findings.Quote: running beneath the fear like the low end under a song
findings.Note: Musical-metaphor-for-emotion is a stock device, and generic here since it doesn't tie to Ethan's specific stage/performer background established earlier.
findings.Fix: Cut simile or ground it more specifically in his musician's ear rather than a generic 'low end under a song.'

findings.Quote: He felt this one close around him like a hand
findings.Note: Same hand-image is reused for the room-sightline sensation and then literally repeated for Koss's hand on Mona's shoulder and later for Faith's silence-catching — the recycled metaphor dilutes rather than reinforces the geometric-outmaneuvering beat.
findings.Fix: Use a distinct image tied to stagecraft/sightlines rather than 'hand' again.

findings.Quote: and it said a third thing the band had been building a wall against for four years, and there wasn't time to read it.
findings.Note: The purpose calls for Mona's look to pay off four years of suppressed feeling, but the text explicitly refuses to deliver or specify it ('there wasn't time to read it'), deferring the payoff instead of landing it.
findings.Fix: Let Ethan register even a fragment of what the look means, rather than waving it off as unreadable.

findings.Quote: the certainty of the next word in your own sentence
findings.Note: abstract aphoristic simile that doesn't clarify the visual/physical fact being described (her turning early)
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete sensory comparison tied to the chase

findings.Quote: the recognition land through him like a plucked string
findings.Note: stock musical-metaphor for emotional/physical response, a common shorthand rather than a specific image
findings.Fix: cut the simile or replace with a concrete physical detail unique to Ethan

findings.Quote: Two more by the side door carrying the weight of something planned, a job being done on a schedule.
findings.Note: the beat is meant to escalate into a forced choice of who to save first, but only Ethan is ever considered — Mona and others are named but no actual triage/choice is dramatized
findings.Fix: show Faith briefly weighing Mona or another target before settling on Ethan, so the 'choose who to save first' stakes register

findings.Quote: because a woman who read a room like that and said nothing was either very careful or very certain, and he needed to know which before the night sorted itself into its usual shapes and left no opening for the question
findings.Fix: trim to a shorter, more concrete want rather than an explanatory aphorism about types of women

findings.Quote: He read her clean. That was the surprise of it — clean as spring water.
findings.Note: 'Clean as spring water' is a soft, pastoral cliché-adjacent simile that clashes tonally with the cyberpunk/violent register of the scene.
findings.Fix: Replace with a starker, register-appropriate comparison or cut the simile.

findings.Quote: It was what you had left when there was nothing else to do.
findings.Note: Generalizing aphoristic aside that tells the reader the emotional function of the gesture instead of trusting the concrete action already shown.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the preceding action already conveys helplessness.

findings.Quote: She laughed.
findings.Note: The purpose centers on exposing Faith's vulnerability and Ethan's guilt via her reading him; ending the beat on Faith's laugh shifts focus to her reaction/performance rather than closing on Ethan's stripped composure, slightly diffusing the intended payoff.
findings.Fix: Hold a beat longer on Ethan's exposed state before pivoting to Faith's laugh, or trim the laugh's buildup so it doesn't overtake the guilt payoff.

findings.Quote: the honest little strip telling its one truth
findings.Note: Cute personification that undercuts the tension of the standoff with a whimsical aside.
findings.Fix: Cut the editorializing clause; let the flat light-strip detail stand alone.

findings.Quote: the sore man at the fire escape, one boot off, one minute of relief
findings.Note: Functions as a stock 'weary soldier taking a breather' image inserted for contrast; reads as generic shorthand rather than earned specific memory.
findings.Fix: Trim or replace with a detail more specific to their shared history.

findings.Quote: a stone dropped in a well with no splash coming back
findings.Note: well/stone-drop is a familiar stock image for absorbed bad news
findings.Fix: replace with a less generic image tied to the story's sensory palette (neuretics, sound, mesh)

findings.Quote: a singer's breath, a man rationing air he didn't know he was rationing
findings.Note: tidy, slightly precious phrasing that tells us the meaning of the breath rather than just showing it
findings.Fix: cut 'he didn't know he was rationing' or simplify to avoid the aphoristic turn

findings.Quote: telling the truth it always told: she wasn't moving. She wasn't going to.
findings.Note: abstract personification of the light-strip undercuts the concrete physical stillness the beat wants to land on
findings.Fix: cut the 'truth it always told' framing; state the stillness plainly

findings.Quote: She held it the way she held the last note of the slow one — past the point where the body starts to argue, past the burn coming up under the ribs, past the white edge of it.
findings.Note: the singing metaphor is doing double duty (also used in ref 1 for Ethan) and here reads as reaching for lyricism mid-crisis rather than embodied panic
findings.Fix: trim to a more physical, less curated comparison or cut the simile

findings.Quote: Too small and too stupid to be a lie.
findings.Note: aphoristic fragment asserting truth-by-assertion rather than demonstrating why the line reads as true
findings.Fix: ground the judgment in a specific physical tell from Ethan

findings.Quote: a door in them you didn't know was there
findings.Note: stock metaphor for hidden depths/secrets
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, non-idiomatic image

findings.Quote: He was aware, distantly, that he ought to be more afraid than this.
findings.Note: beat purpose is to build Ethan's dawning awareness of Faith's ability, but this line pivots attention to his own fear-numbness rather than her uncanniness, slightly diffusing focus
findings.Fix: cut or tie the numbness directly back to his growing awareness of her control

findings.Quote: which was stupid — nothing down here could hear her. Except everything up here could hear *them*, and she'd stopped being able to tell the two directions apart.
findings.Note: the up/down direction wordplay is muddled and reads as clever filler rather than clarifying her state of mind
findings.Fix: simplify to a direct sensory beat about the danger of noise

findings.Quote: a man pouring himself through a slot the world had cut a size too small
findings.Note: overwrought action-hero phrasing for a simple climbing-through-a-gap action
findings.Fix: trim to plainer physical description

findings.Quote: close enough that close was a fact and not a question
findings.Note: clever-sounding wordplay that doesn't clarify the physical staging, reads as a phrase admiring itself
findings.Fix: state the actual distance/action instead of the abstraction

findings.Quote: Her heartbeat picked up. She set it down again, hard.
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific physical or behavioral beat to avoid the stock heartbeat cue

findings.Quote: Land her.
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a less blunt/cliché term for the goal

findings.Quote: the engine still running with no road left to put it on
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a more literal physical detail

findings.Quote: he'd feel every one of his thirty-six years land at once
findings.Fix: cut the aphoristic framing; show a specific ache instead

findings.Quote: His pulse ticked in his throat
findings.Fix: replace with a less stock physical marker of adrenaline crash

findings.Quote: Rill was quiet all the way down.
findings.Fix: cut or ground in a concrete behavioral detail rather than a summarizing aphorism
